s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and mass with acute exacerbation
salient_findings: Palpable, movable mass in the upper abdomen
Large echogenic mass in the gastric antrum on ultrasound
Large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall on endoscopy
key_facts: 63-year-old woman
Insidious upper abdominal pain unrelated to food ingestion
Nausea
Episode of intense acute abdominal pain
No hematemesis or melena
Untreated dyslipidemia
Well-controlled hypertension on methyldopa
Smoker of ten cigarettes per day
No family history of cancer
Normal physical examination except for abdominal mass
Normal laboratory tests, including complete blood count
No anemia
Abdominal ultrasound showed large echogenic mass in gastric antrum
Endoscopy revealed large submucosal bulging mass in posterior gastric wall
Biopsy attempts failed to sample submucosal mass
Ulcer biopsies showed only necrotic mucosa
Contrast-enhanced CT showed well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass arising from posterior gastric wall

differentials: Gastric inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor with anaplastic lymphoma kinase rearrangement
per_call: Gastric inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor with anaplastic lymphoma kinase rearrangement

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Large submucosal bulging mass in posterior gastric wall with ulcerated areas

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass with fat-tissue attenuation and trabecular architecture

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass with fat-tissue attenuation on CT scan

shortlist.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Episode of intense acute abdominal pain and ulcerated areas

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large mass with potential for malignancy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall with ulcerated areas and the imaging findings of a well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass with fat-tissue attenuation and central contrast enhancement are consistent with a gastrointestinal stromal tumor.

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: Less likely due to the presence of ulcerated areas and the large size of the mass

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Imaging findings do not support a lipoma, as the mass has central contrast enhancement and a trabecular architecture

rejected.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The mass is described as a submucosal bulging mass with ulcerated areas, but the biopsy attempts failed to sample the submucosal mass and only showed necrotic mucosa, making gastric adenocarcinoma less likely

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The imaging findings and the presence of a well-defined, homogeneous mass are not typical of leiomyosarcoma, which is usually more aggressive and heterogeneous
